$comment: Capability-coverage ratchet for the platform test checklist. The universe of governed metadata kinds is DERIVED at check time from packages/spec/liveness/*.json (the ADR-0049 ledger set) — this file must map EVERY kind to at least one checklist item, or waive it with a reason. scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs flags both directions: an unmapped kind (the platform grew a capability the checklist doesn't test) and an entry for a kind with no liveness ledger (orphan, mirrors the liveness ORPHAN discipline). NOTE: this check runs on a MANUAL/periodic cadence (`pnpm check:platform-checklist`), not in per-PR CI — see docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md 'Operating cadence'. Pattern copied from examples/app-showcase/src/coverage.ts (demonstrated-or-waived, ADR-0060 house ledger style). NOT ALL of the universe is a metadata KIND: check-liveness.mts enrols a few SPEC-ONLY schemas (query, qa, manifest, the four RestServerConfig sub-objects, the realtime SubscriptionSchema) through its SPEC_ONLY_SCHEMAS override, and each gets a liveness ledger like any governed kind — so this map is keyed by LEDGER NAME, and an entry here may describe a deployment construction argument or a transport-protocol schema rather than a stored metadata row.

assignment_rule.waived: WAIVED 2026-10-26 — no fixture declares one yet, measured rather than asserted. The runtime landed with ADR-0142 phase 2 (#25769): the engine routes each inserted row with no owner and no queue through the object's declared `assignmentRules` (park in a queue, `round_robin` or `least_loaded`), and `POST /security/_activation/assignment_rule/:name` switches one off. It is proven by unit and integration suites (packages/objectql/src/ownership-queue.test.ts, the runtime activation-door test), but no app this checklist drives (the showcase, the dev apps) declares an assignment rule, so an item written to RUN today has nothing to route. WHAT RETIRES THIS WAIVER — an app the checklist drives declares a queue and an assignment rule (the HotCRM adoption phase of #25769); an item then inserts a matching record and reads where it went (parked, or owned by the member the strategy chose), and the same edit replaces this waiver with `items` naming it. ⚠️ Re-audit it every sweep, as SWEEP.md asks of every waiver. Re-audited 2026-11-10 by scoped sweep #32019 (framework 60f8149e): access-security.sharing-queue-assignment-package-resolution now declares an assignment rule in two scratch packages, but only to drive the activation door's 409 for a name two packages hold. It inserts no record and reads no routing, so the premise above still holds and the waiver stands.

picklist.$comment: Re-audited 2026-10-27 (the checklist-author pass on QA run #26715, framework 43731031): the 2026-09-30 waiver is STALE and is replaced by items, as SWEEP.md asks of every waiver. Its premise was that no runtime reads a picklist, packages/spec/liveness/picklist.json grading every key planned. At 43731031 that ledger grades 10 of its 11 keys live, verified 2026-10-01: the ObjectQL registry resolves a list onto every field that names it and merges picklistExtensions additively (packages/objectql/src/picklist-resolution.ts; the name row's evidence is packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, resolvePicklistOptions), and an ACTIVE item drives that runtime end to end: studio-authoring.picklist-bound-select (since v17.7) reads GET /meta/picklist, the served options with the extension's option, the bound field's PUT round-trip and both objects' forms. What the mapping does NOT claim: that item's fixture is an uncommitted checkout edit (the stock showcase declares no picklist and the kind is code-only, so no runtime door mints one), and QA run #26715 scored it blocked(fixture) because the run did not make the edit; the coverage is real but costs a run that edit. records-forms.picklist-shared-across-objects stays PLANNED and is listed as the map target the waiver named; it contributes zero, and its promotion still needs a passing run of its own.

queue.waived: WAIVED 2026-10-26 — no fixture declares one yet, measured rather than asserted. The runtime landed with ADR-0142 phase 2 (#25769): the `queue` column on `ownership: 'user'` objects, the sitting-record read/edit path for queue members, claim / release / move through the owner gate (409 for the losing claimant, 422 QUEUE_NOT_FOUND), the `queue` sharing recipient and the `queue` approver. It is proven by unit and integration suites (plugin-sharing ownership-queue tests, the plugin-security queue gate and explain tests, the approvals queue tests), but no app this checklist drives (the showcase, the dev apps) declares a queue, and the console has no queue surface yet, so an item written to RUN today has no queue to claim from. WHAT RETIRES THIS WAIVER — an app the checklist drives declares a staffed queue (the HotCRM adoption phase of #25769); items then drive claim (two members race, one wins), release, move and the member-only read across two personas, and the same edit replaces this waiver with `items` naming them. ⚠️ Re-audit it every sweep, as SWEEP.md asks of every waiver. Re-audited 2026-11-10 by scoped sweep #32019 (framework 60f8149e): access-security.sharing-queue-assignment-package-resolution now declares a queue in two scratch packages, but only to drive the activation door's 409 for a name two packages hold. It stages no queue member and drives no claim, release, move or member-only read, so the premise above still holds for those and the waiver stands.

realtime_subscription.waived: WAIVED 2026-09-04 — there is no runtime behaviour to drive, measured rather than asserted. SubscriptionSchema (packages/spec/src/api/realtime.zod.ts) is a TRANSPORT-PROTOCOL declaration with zero runtime readers: its liveness ledger records every property dead at a same-day census, nothing outside packages/spec imports SubscriptionSchema / SubscriptionEventSchema / RealtimeConfigSchema, and the shipped in-memory adapter reads a different type entirely (RealtimeSubscriptionOptions, packages/spec/src/contracts/realtime-service.ts). There is also nothing for a client to connect to: measured on a stock showcase boot for #14646, GET /api/v1/discovery reports realtime enabled:true but status degraded, handlerReady:false, and no realtime entry in the routes map — #14646 is the open decision on whether the open framework mounts an HTTP/WS/SSE realtime surface at all. An item authored today could only assert absence, which belongs in FOLLOW-UPS.md (§10) and on #14646, not in a coverage entry. WHAT RETIRES THIS WAIVER — either the #14646 decision mounts a realtime transport that parses this schema, in which case author the subscribe / unsubscribe / event-delivery contract and flip this entry to items; or the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove call retires the schema and its ledger, and the ratchet flags this entry as an ORPHAN to delete. ⚠️ Re-audit it every sweep: 6 of 6 waivers ever written in this file turned out stale (SWEEP.md), which is why this one is grounded in the census and the discovery reading rather than in the schema's own prose.

rest_api.$comment: Mapped 2026-09-21 (#14640) when RestApiConfigSchema — the FIFTH RestServerConfig sub-object — was enrolled as a liveness ledger, which is what put this kind in the ratchet's universe. ⚠️ READ WHAT THESE TWO ITEMS DO AND DO NOT COVER, because it is narrower than the three sibling `api-backend.rest-*-config-contract` items and pretending otherwise is the manufactured-coverage failure this file exists to stop. COVERED, on the DEFAULT config: route-ledger-live-parity boots the real stack and fires a representative route per family — discovery, openapi, metadata, ui, crud, batch, search — so the eight `enable*` switches are observed at their default (on) values by the mounts they gate, and every probe addresses `{apiPath}/…`; qa-suite-execution derives that prefix from RestApiConfigSchema's own `apiPath ?? {basePath}/{version}` and memoises a `/discovery` probe per run, so `version` / `basePath` / `apiPath` are exercised as the contract rather than as a literal. NOT COVERED: the NON-DEFAULT variants. The three sibling sub-objects each have a dedicated item that constructs a RestServer with a non-default block in a scratch vitest harness and reads getRoutes() back; the `api` sub-object has no such item, so `enableCrud: false` mounting nothing, a moved `apiPath`, and `projectResolution` deciding whether the unscoped legacy routes mount alongside the scoped ones are all unverified. An `api-backend.rest-api-config-contract` item on the siblings' shape is the gap, and it is authoring work with its own measurement, not a line in this file. ALSO NOT COVERED, and deliberately not a waiver: `api.documentation` and `api.responseFormat` are `dead` in the ledger — normalized and read by nothing — so there is no behaviour to drive; the enforce-or-remove call on them (ADR-0049) is a follow-up on the human floor, and whichever way it goes is what gives them a testable surface. ⛔ Not mapped to enforce-or-remove-authoring-gates, although route_generation is: this schema's `requireAuth` tombstone is `.omit()`ed by the REST seam on purpose (#3963 chose warn-and-ignore), so it does NOT refuse at construction the way that item's samples do — the tombstone that does refuse is the STACK-side twin, a different key on a different schema.

template_manifest.waived: WAIVED 2026-11-06 — no item in this checklist can drive it, measured rather than asserted. TemplateManifestSchema (packages/spec/src/marketplace/template-manifest.zod.ts) is `objectstack.manifest.json`, the package-listing file; its one runtime reader is `os package publish` (packages/cli/src/commands/package/publish.ts), whose every request goes to a HOSTED control plane (`/api/v1/cloud/packages`) that a local app booted for this checklist does not serve, and its other reader is create-objectstack at scaffold time. The CLI half is pinned where it can fail: packages/cli/test/package-publish-taxonomy.test.ts (the retired `category` refused before any network call, each facet judged and sent under its wire name, the solutionType cross-check against the built artifact) and packages/cli/test/package-publish-uncarried-manifest-keys.test.ts (every schema key sent, warned about, refused or scaffold-only); every shipped file is parsed by `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:template-manifests`. The catalog half — storing, filtering and showing the facets — is the cloud checklist's (objectstack-ai/cloud#3661) and the console marketplace card's. WHAT RETIRES THIS WAIVER — the console marketplace card lands facet filters this checklist can drive against a catalog it can boot, in which case author the browse-and-filter item and flip this entry to items.

releaseSweeps.$comment: Release-sweep close-out ledger (#32270). No gate reads it: scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs and scripts/checklist-select.mjs read metadataKinds only, so this is not coverage and never waives a kind. Per release wave it answers two questions for the release-candidate run and the next sweep. `themes`: every theme of the wave's epic, its items, and for each item no run can drive yet (`blocked`) or that names a capability not landed (`planned`), why. `packages`: every workspace package changed since the subject that no bearing item's source[] cited when the close-out began, and either the items that cite it now or why it needs none (`internal-only`, `test-only`, or `covered-through` named items). A new release wave adds its own key beside v18.4.
